starting-point.title: Choose your starting point
starting-point.goal: Choose the version you will improve: your own Part 3 baseline, or the Practice task baseline.
why: Every round compares a changed prompt with a starting version, so you choose the starting version first.

Your Part 3 baseline is your own work: your prompt, your rules, your checker and your five answers. The Practice task baseline is a ready-made set for the Practice task. It is for practice only, it cannot be submitted, and it never touches your own files.
If your own baseline already scores 95% or more, there is little to improve in it. The Practice task baseline gives you something to improve either way.
This is this course's way of working. Other approaches to improving a prompt work too.
instructions: Read both choices. Nothing is chosen for you.
Press Use my Part 3 baseline, or press Use the Practice task baseline.
Your choice is fixed once round 1 begins. To use the other one, reset your lesson progress in Settings. Your files are kept.

known-good.title: Check your checker
known-good.goal: Write a known-good answer from your written requirements and confirm your checker scores it 95% or more.
why: A checker you have not tested can be wrong in either direction. A known-good answer clearly meets every requirement, so a checker you can trust should pass it.

Choose it from the written requirements before you see its score. Never pick the strongest of your five answers: that would test the checker against the answers you already have and not against the requirements.
The checker should score it 95% or more. If it does not, investigate the checker or the written requirements. Do not loosen a rule just to make it pass.
This check is separate from the five-answer score. The two are never merged.
This is this course's way of working. Other approaches to improving a prompt work too.
instructions: Read your written requirements below.
Write or paste one answer that clearly meets every requirement. Choose it now, before you see any score.
Press Save and check my answer. The app runs your checker on it, with no AI. The score appears only after the answer is saved.
If the score is under 95%, check the checker or the written requirements, fix the cause and save your answer again. Do not loosen a rule.
If a repair changed what your five original answers score, press Run my five original answers again before you start a round.

hypothesis-1.title: Round 1: Write your hypothesis
hypothesis-1.goal: Say which rule you want to move and what you expect your change to do, before you change anything.
why: A hypothesis is a prediction written before the result. One written after the result is only a story.
Look at every rule of your starting version, not only the total. A total can hide a rule that fails.
Name one rule and say what you expect. One change, one hypothesis.
Your text stays editable until the round has a saved answer. After that it cannot change, because a hypothesis written after the result is not a prediction.
This is this course's way of working. Other approaches to improving a prompt work too.
instructions: Read the result of Iteration 0 for each rule. Any rule that does not pass every answer is marked in words.
Write one hypothesis: the rule you want to move and what you expect. For example: naming the exact labels I want will move the rule that checks labels from 3 of 5 to 5 of 5.
Press Save my hypothesis. The next step opens.

troubleshooting.problem: You are not sure which rule to pick.
troubleshooting.fix: Pick a rule that does not pass every answer. If every rule passes every answer, pick the rule you care about most and predict that it stays at 5 of 5.

measure-1.title: Round 1: Collect and score five answers
measure-1.line: Read prompt.md, follow it, and save only your answer to output.txt. Do nothing else.
measure-1.folder_label: Folder with only this round's prompt
measure-1.goal: Collect five fresh answers from this round's prompt, then let the app score them with your checker.
why: Five answers give a steadier rate than one, because the model varies from run to run. Each answer is a new chat, so no answer can remember an earlier one.
The app starts your AI on the model chosen with the Sonnet / Haiku switch and records it. Keep the model the same from round to round, so the only difference is your change.
The app scores the five answers by running your checker itself, with no AI call.
Read every rule, not only the total. A total can rise while a rule gets worse, and a rule that becomes NOT CHECKED is lost coverage and never a gain.
The 95% score is a target and not a gate. Below it you get a suggested next step, and you can still finish the round.
This is this course's way of working. Other approaches to improving a prompt work too.
instructions: Your AI window opens by itself the first time you open this step, in a folder that holds only this round's prompt. If it did not open, press Open a new AI chat.
If your AI asks whether to trust the folder, choose the yes option. The highlighted default may be No.
Wait until your AI is ready for a message. Press Copy, click in the AI window, paste with {paste_key} and press Enter. Do not add anything.
The app waits for output.txt, saves it as the next answer and closes your AI window.
For each of answers 2 to 5, press Open a new AI chat, wait until it is ready, then copy and paste the line again. One prompt, one answer, one new chat each time.
When all five answers are saved, press Score these five answers.
Read the table. Every rule shows its count before and after. Keeping or undoing the round is your decision in the next step.

decide-1.goal: Keep or undo this round, then record it in your iteration log.
why: Keeping or undoing is your decision and not the app's. The latest round is not kept unless you keep it.
An undone round stays in the log, marked undone. What you tried and what happened is part of the record.
Your AI writes the numbers and your saved hypothesis. You write the Change, the Result, the Reasoning and the Decision line in your own words. The app only reads the log and never changes it.
One comparison is an observation: it can suggest and it never proves. The score says nothing about qualities no rule checks.

After you decide, the app says whether the round showed a measured gain on these rules. An equal or lower score is no measured gain on these rules, and a simpler prompt at the same score can still be worth keeping.
This is this course's way of working. Other approaches to improving a prompt work too.
instructions: Read the results above, then press Keep this round or Undo this round.

After you decide, a line to paste appears and your AI window opens by itself. Wait until it is ready, press Copy, click in the AI window, paste with {paste_key} and press Enter. It adds the numbers and your saved hypothesis to the log file named above the line.
Open that log file in your editor. Under the entry for this round, write the Change, the Result, the Reasoning and a Decision line (kept or undone) in your own words.
Press Check my work.

This is this course's way of working. Other approaches to improving a prompt work too.
instructions: Read the result of the version you kept for each rule. Any rule that does not pass every answer is marked in words.
Write one hypothesis: the rule you want to move and what you expect. For example: naming the exact labels I want will move the rule that checks labels from 3 of 5 to 5 of 5.
Press Save my hypothesis. The next step opens.

troubleshooting.fix: Pick a rule that does not pass every answer. If every rule passes every answer, pick the rule you care about most and predict that it stays at 5 of 5.

why: Change one thing at a time. If you change two things and the score moves, you cannot tell which one did it.
This is this round's own copy. Your earlier prompts, rules, checker and answers are not touched.
Keep the input, the model and the rules the same, so the only difference is your change.

measure-3.title: Round 3 (optional): Collect and score five answers
measure-3.line: Read prompt.md, follow it, and save only your answer to output.txt. Do nothing else.
measure-3.folder_label: Folder with only this round's prompt
measure-3.goal: Collect five fresh answers from this round's prompt, then let the app score them with your checker.
why: Five answers give a steadier rate than one, because the model varies from run to run. Each answer is a new chat, so no answer can remember an earlier one.
The app starts your AI on the model chosen with the Sonnet / Haiku switch and records it. Keep the model the same from round to round, so the only difference is your change.
The app scores the five answers by running your checker itself, with no AI call.
Read every rule, not only the total. A total can rise while a rule gets worse, and a rule that becomes NOT CHECKED is lost coverage and never a gain.
The 95% score is a target and not a gate. Below it you get a suggested next step, and you can still finish the round.
This is this course's way of working. Other approaches to improving a prompt work too.
instructions: Your AI window opens by itself the first time you open this step, in a folder that holds only this round's prompt. If it did not open, press Open a new AI chat.
If your AI asks whether to trust the folder, choose the yes option. The highlighted default may be No.
Wait until your AI is ready for a message. Press Copy, click in the AI window, paste with {paste_key} and press Enter. Do not add anything.
The app waits for output.txt, saves it as the next answer and closes your AI window.
For each of answers 2 to 5, press Open a new AI chat, wait until it is ready, then copy and paste the line again. One prompt, one answer, one new chat each time.
When all five answers are saved, press Score these five answers.
Read the table. Every rule shows its count before and after. Keeping or undoing the round is your decision in the next step.

troubleshooting.fix: Wait a moment and ask it again in the AI window. If it keeps failing, press Open a new AI chat, wait until it is ready, then copy and paste the line again.

troubleshooting.fix: Look at the AI window. If your AI is set to ask for approval, it may be waiting for you. Answer it there.

troubleshooting.fix: The app needs a file called output.txt with text in it. If your AI printed the answer but saved nothing, press Open a new AI chat, wait until it is ready, then copy and paste the line again.

decide-3.goal: Keep or undo this round, then record it in your iteration log.
why: Keeping or undoing is your decision and not the app's. The latest round is not kept unless you keep it.
An undone round stays in the log, marked undone. What you tried and what happened is part of the record.
Your AI writes the numbers and your saved hypothesis. You write the Change, the Result, the Reasoning and the Decision line in your own words. The app only reads the log and never changes it.
One comparison is an observation: it can suggest and it never proves. The score says nothing about qualities no rule checks.

After you decide, the app says whether the round showed a measured gain on these rules. An equal or lower score is no measured gain on these rules, and a simpler prompt at the same score can still be worth keeping.
This is this course's way of working. Other approaches to improving a prompt work too.
instructions: Read the results above, then press Keep this round or Undo this round.

After you decide, a line to paste appears and your AI window opens by itself. Wait until it is ready, press Copy, click in the AI window, paste with {paste_key} and press Enter. It adds the numbers and your saved hypothesis to the log file named above the line.
Open that log file in your editor. Under the entry for this round, write the Change, the Result, the Reasoning and a Decision line (kept or undone) in your own words.
Press Check my work.

troubleshooting.problem: The line to paste is not shown.
troubleshooting.fix: It appears after you keep or undo the round.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the Decision differs.
troubleshooting.fix: Your log must say the same thing you chose in the app: kept or undone. Fix the Decision line in the log file. The app never edits your log.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says the counts differ.
troubleshooting.fix: The app's count comes from running your checker itself, so trust it over the log. Ask your AI to correct the entry, or fix the number in the log file.

troubleshooting.problem: The app says your Change, Result or Reasoning is missing.
troubleshooting.fix: Write them in your own words under this round's entry in the log file. The app checks only that they are there.

troubleshooting.problem: The log has two entries for this round.
troubleshooting.fix: Keep one. Open the log file, delete the older entry and press Check my work again.
